articles.title: Shooter Climbing Steam Charts Lists 10 Reasons Not To Buy It
articles.title_tr: Shooter Climbing Steam Charts Lists 10 Reasons Not To Buy It
articles.summary:
Wardogs, an upcoming large-scale, hardcore FPS inspired by games like Arma, is taking a unique approach with its marketing by listing 10 reasons why prospective players shouldn't buy it.



In an official video, developer Bulkhead revealed September 10 as Wardogs' Steam early access release date, but also laid the rest of its cards on the table. Point by point, it outlined all the main reasons why potential players might not want to take a chance on the shooter, ranging from its lack of content, high early-access price, visual fidelity, and even the failure of Bulkhead's previous shooter, Battalion: 1944. 



"Before the hype train gets out of control, we want to do something most AAA marketing teams would tell their dev teams to never do--give you 10 legitimate reasons why you should not buy Wardogs," Bulkhead said in the video.



Those reasons are as follows:




Lack of early-access content



Early-access pricing



Player count will decline



Monetization



Performance and visuals



Shifting early-access priorities



Battalion: 1944



VOIP



Controller support



Decisions and consequences





https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ugkuP4a3xk4




Some of those reasons are fairly self explanatory, like lack of content during the early-access period and its price. Wardogs will initially cost $40 in early access, a steep price for some. The price will go up over the course of development and will eventually sell for $60 at the end of early access.



"If the price sounds too high for an early-access game, please don't buy it yet," Bulkhead said.



Other reasons require a bit more explanation. Decisions and consequences refers to Wardog's more milsim-style gameplay, where death requires a long trek back to the frontlines and rebuying lost equipment. 



"If you're running in like you're playing Call of Duty or Battlefield, you will likely die to someone playing more cautiously," Bulkhead said. "If you're not willing to learn from those deaths, you're going to have a bad time."  



While Wardogs doesn't yet have any monetization like a battle pass or paid skins, there will eventually be some way for Bulkhead to make more money and continue funding the game's development. However, that will likely be years from now, as Bulkhead said it won't monetize the game during early access. Additionally, Bulkhead won't sell weapon camos or in-game currency, with players needing to earn them through play.



"It might seem strange to be talking about monetization years down the line, but we want you to be able to buy in knowing what you're buying into long term," Bulkhead said.



One of the most hard-hitting reasons is Bulkhead's track record. The team previously released Battalion: 1944, a 5v5 Call of Duty-inspired shooter that died almost immediately on release, having only ever reached between 50-200 concurrent players, Bulkhead said. The studio eventually saved enough funds from work-for-hire projects to stay afloat, offered refunds to players, and refunded Battalion: 1944's Kickstarter backers, but it understands why some players may be hesitant.



"It's these lessons and scars from Battalion that Wardogs has been built upon," Bulkhead said. "It's why we've been so cautious with our playtesting and why we've been so open with our marketing. To be really clear, we wouldn't have Wardogs without Battalion's failure, but if you still don't trust our studio because of Battalion: 1944, don't rush to buy Wardogs."



So far, Bulkhead's list of reasons don't seem to be slowing down Wardogs' sales. It's currently climbing up Steam top-seller charts.

articles.title_tr: Başsavcılık'tan CHP'li Yazgan için soruşturma kararı
articles.summary:
CHP Edirne Milletvekili Ahmet Baran Yazgan hakkında sosyal medyada yayılan görüntü ve iddialar üzerine Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca soruşturma başlatıldı. Başsavcılık, Yazgan hakkında "cinsel taciz" ve "sarkıntılık düzeyinde kalan cinsel saldırı" suçlarından soruşturma yürütüldüğünü duyurdu.Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, CHP Edirne Milletvekili Ahmet Baran Yazgan hakkında sosyal medyada yayılan görüntü ve iddialar üzerine soruşturma başlatıldığını açıkladı.

13 Ağustos tarihli açıklamada, Yazgan'la ilgili görüntü içerikleri ve iddialar nedeniyle 5237 sayılı Türk Ceza Kanunu'nun 105/1. maddesinde düzenlenen "cinsel taciz" ile 102/1-2. cümlesinde düzenlenen "sarkıntılık düzeyinde kalan cinsel saldırı" suçlarından re'sen soruşturma başlatıldığı belirtildi.

NE OLMUŞTU?

CHP Edirne Milletvekili Ahmet Baran Yazgan'ın Edirne'de bir evde bulunduğu sırada çıkan tartışmanın kavgaya dönüştüğü ve Yazgan'ın darbedildiği görüntüler sosyal medyada yayıldı.

İddialara göre tartışma, Yazgan'ın evde bulunan kadınlara yönelik tacizde bulunduğu iddiası üzerine başladı. Olay sırasında bir kadın ve bir erkeğin Yazgan'ı darbettiği anlar cep telefonu görüntülerine yansıdı.

Tarafların olayın ardından karşılıklı olarak şikâyetçi olduğu öğrenildi. Yazgan darbedildiği gerekçesiyle şikâyetçi olurken, karşı taraf Yazgan hakkında taciz, tehdit ve hakaret iddialarıyla suç duyurusunda bulundu.

3 KİŞİ GÖZALTINA ALINMIŞTI

Olayla ilgili soruşturma kapsamında 2'si kadın 3 kişi gözaltına alındı.

Şüpheliler B.Ş. (33), T.A. (33) ve N.D. (39), emniyetteki işlemlerinin ardından Edirne Adliyesi'ne sevk edildi.

Şüphelilerin ifadelerinde, doğum günü kutlamasının ardından T.A.'nın evine gittikleri ve Yazgan ile balkonda alkol aldıkları, daha sonra çıkan tartışmanın kavgaya dönüştüğü iddia edildi.

Şüpheliler de Yazgan'dan cinsel taciz, tehdit ve hakaret iddialarıyla şikâyetçi oldu.

CHP GENEL MERKEZİ'NE ÇAĞRILMIŞTI

Sosyal medyada görüntülerin yayılmasının ardından CHP'deki butlan yönetiminin Parti Sözcüsü Müslim Sarı, Yazgan'ın Genel Merkez'e çağrıldığını açıklamıştı.

Sarı, "Edirne Milletvekilimiz Ahmet Baran Yazgan, konunun tüm yönleriyle araştırılması için CHP Genel Merkezi'ne çağrılmıştır" ifadelerini kullanmıştı.

Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı'nın son açıklamasıyla birlikte Yazgan hakkında ayrıca cinsel taciz ve cinsel saldırı suçlamaları yönünden adli soruşturma başlatılmış oldu.

articles.title: Marvel Tokon Nears 500K Sales In Its First Week Despite Fighting Games’ Niche Appeal
articles.title_tr: Marvel Tokon Nears 500K Sales In Its First Week Despite Fighting Games’ Niche Appeal
articles.summary:
A week has passed since Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls launched for PC and PS5, and the new fighting game is off to a solid start. According to new estimates by Alinea Analytics, the game has reportedly sold 485,000 units as of August 12, with PS5 being the dominant platform.



As outlined by Alinea Analytics’ head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, the PS5 accounted for 74% of sales, and Steam 26%. That's not too surprising, as the game experienced technical issues on PC. Developer Arc System Works released a patch for Marvel Tokon earlier this week, aiming to address multiple performance issues on PC.



Those sales account for an estimated $33 million in revenue, and Elliott also noted that only 15.1% of the units sold on PS5 were physical copies, which is surprisingly low for a new PlayStation game. Further analysis showed that Marvel Tokon attracted a crowd of hardcore fighting game fans, as 52% of people had previously played Arc's Dragon Ball FighterZ, 39% had played Street Fighter 6, and 41% had played Mortal Kombat 1.



Image credit: Alinea Analytics



Marvel fans also helped drive sales, as there's a strong crossover here with people who had previously played games like Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man titles and NetEase's Marvel Rivals. With Spider-Man: Brand New Day doing blockbuster numbers at cinemas, it's not too hard to imagine having Spider-Man in a new fighting game would also attarct potential customers--or boost sales, like in the case of Marvel's Spider-Man 2.



Being close to 500,000 sales might not sound that impressive, but as Elliott explained, fighting games are still a niche genre. What they do have going for them are passionate fanbases, giving these games long legs over time.



To give you an idea, Street Fighter 6 has cleared 7 million lifetime sales as of June 30, 2026. The game first launched in 2023 and is easily the fighting game of the current generation, so Marvel Tokon has its work cut out for it if it wants to dethrones Capcom popular brawler.



The brand recognition of Marvel certainly helps, and the developers of Marvel Tokon have an ambitious goal to keep this 4v4 fighting game in the spotlight for the next decade. 



"Marvel heroes and villains are once again beating each other up in tag-based battles, and I am loving the experience of jumping in and figuring out new strategies," Jason Fanelli wrote in GameSpot's Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls review. "Rather than lean on old tropes, Arc System Works elected to put its own spin on the idea, and what they've cooked up sets a new bar for future tag fighters. Once the technical issues for PC are ironed out, there's a bright future ahead. With Marvel Tokon, Arc System Works has created the next foundational title for modern fighting games."
